run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T13:14:13Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by real error spans on that service: frontend-proxy 'ingress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans rose from ~0.015/s at 13:14:13 to ~1.04/s at 13:21:13 and returned to baseline by ~13:29:13, and the failing ingress spans carry HTTP 504/503 (and 500) at the proxy's 15s timeout. Those 5xx are the proxy's view of failures in its upstream frontend: frontend's own spans show HTTP 500 on 'GET /api/data' whose exception is 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds ... 14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' (the ad Service ClusterIP), and the slow 504 traces show frontend /api/data (21.36s) waiting on ad's 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' server span (20.77s), which itself was consumed by 12 flag-resolution child spans of 0.7-4.4s each. The deepest supporting cause is on the ad workload: its pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh (created by Deployment ad's rollout restart at 13:15:33Z, same image, restartCount 0) burned up to 0.0493 cores against a 50m CPU limit and was CFS-throttled 96.9-99.2% of periods from 13:17:13 through 13:23:13, the highest throttling of any pod at that instant, whereas the previous ad pod used 0.005-0.008 cores at 9-32% throttling. ad's GetAds p95 went from 88-103ms (13:09-13:19) to 390ms then 6834ms at 13:25:13, which is exactly the latency that pushed frontend/proxy past the 15s timeout. flagd is not the origin of the delay: its container used a flat ~0.0028 cores with 0% CFS throttling, its ResolveBoolean handler spans were 25-112us, and its only errors are 'context deadline exceeded' on requests whose client side had already waited seconds; node conditions are clean on all 5 nodes. What made the new ad container demand ~6-10x the CPU of its predecessor could not be determined because the live flagd flag state and change history are not readable here.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's own error-span rate (span_name='ingress' and 'router frontend egress', status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR) was ~0.0148/s at 13:14:13, jumped to 0.211/s at 13:17:13, peaked at 1.037/s at 13:21:13 and fell back to 0.0148/s at 13:29:13, while its total span rate stayed ~12.6/s.

frontend-proxy ingress error spans observed at 13:22:54-13:25:02 carry http.status_code 504 (4 spans, ~15.0s duration each) and 503 (1 span, 559ms), with the matching 'router frontend egress' spans carrying error=true and http.status_code 0; these are the proxy timing out / failing on its frontend upstream.

The frontend service was itself failing: its error-span rate was 3.75/s at 13:23:13 (vs frontend-proxy 1.53/s) and the error spans are frontend 'GET' (http 500), 'GET /api/data' (500), 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' (500) and 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' with rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and grpc.error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080'.

100.70.197.56 is the clusterIP of Service ad in namespace otel-demo (selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad, port 8080), and the Endpoints object for 'ad' addresses pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh at 100.96.3.224:8080, so the refused/failed calls are to the ad service.

In the timed-out traces the chain is proxy→frontend→ad: frontend-proxy ingress 504 at 15.000154s, frontend 'GET /api/data' 21.356626s, frontend client 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' 21.355726s, and ad server span 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' 20.771412s; ad's duration was consumed by 12 'resolve'/'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean' child spans of 0.700-4.400s each (plus 'getAdsByCategory' at 44-337us).

ad's GetAds p95 latency (histogram_quantile over traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket) was 148-191ms at 12:55-13:07, 88-103ms at 13:09-13:19, then 390ms at 13:21:13 and 6834.63ms at 13:25:13, and ad's GetAds completion rate fell to 0/s at 13:23:13 while requests were still in flight.

The new ad pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh consumed up to 0.04929 cores (its limit is 50m = 0.05) and was CFS-throttled 0.969-0.992 of periods at 13:17:13-13:23:13, falling to 0.266-0.300 by 13:29-13:33; the previous ad pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc used only 0.0050-0.0080 cores with throttling 0.09-0.32.

At 13:23:13 the ad pod had by far the highest CFS throttling of any pod (ad-785b4464f5-9bshh 0.992 vs cart 0.411, frontend 0.282, fraud-detection 0.263, postgresql 0.216, product-catalog 0.216), and the ad container's CPU limit is 50m (request 10m) while the pod is on node i-040b429451d033123 with restartCount 0.

Deployment ad in otel-demo was rolled out at 2026-11-16T13:15:33Z (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-16T13:15:33Z, same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad): ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5 (owner Deployment ad) was scaled 0→1, pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh scheduled/started at 13:15:33-13:15:35 and ad-554b849958 scaled 1→0 with its pod deleted at 13:15:35, so the restart is controller-driven, not a crash.

Verification of entity scope: at 13:23:13 the only services with non-zero STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate were frontend-proxy (1.53/s: 'ingress' 0.769/s, 'router frontend egress' 0.761/s) and frontend (3.75/s: 'GET' 0.993/s, 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' 0.761/s, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' 0.993/s, 'GET /api/data' 0.993/s, 'tcp.connect' 0.015/s); no other service name in traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned a positive error rate.
All 5 nodes report Ready=True with NetworkUnavailable, MemoryPressure, DiskPressure and PIDPressure all False (4 CPU allocatable each), so no node pressure condition existed at query time.

The deployed flag source ConfigMap flagd-config (created 2026-11-16T12:43:26Z, data key demo.flagd.json) defines flags including adFailure defaultVariant 'on', and adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, productCatalogFailure, paymentFailure etc. defaultVariant 'off'; this is the ConfigMap default, not proof of the live flag values flagd served.

The ad container's stdout in 13:15:30-13:26:23 shows routine request handling ('Targeted ad request received for [...]', 'Non-targeted ad request received', 'no baggage found in context') in the newest 40 of 340 lines; only that slice was visible, so it neither proves nor disproves an application-level error.

flagd is not the origin of the added latency: its container held a flat ~0.0028-0.0029 cores over the whole window with CFS throttling exactly 0 at every sampled point (including 13:17-13:33), while its gRPC handler spans ('flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean') took only 25-112us; its error spans only say otel.status_description 'context deadline exceeded', and the corresponding ad client span had already been open for ~2.6s before flagd's handler span started, so the wait was on the ad side / before flagd processed the call.

A cluster-wide/node-level resource cause is not supported: the ad pod's 0.992 throttling at 13:23:13 is far above every other pod on the same node (cart 0.411, frontend 0.282, frontend-proxy 0.045, product-catalog 0.216) and frontend-proxy/frontend themselves show only low, steady throttling through the burst; node conditions show no pressure.

The adFailure feature flag (defaultVariant 'on' in the flagd-config ConfigMap) as the explanation of the observed frontend/proxy failures: ad's own GetAds spans completed with rpc.grpc.status_code 0 and frontend 'GET /api/data' spans completed with http 200 in the same traces, while the failing calls failed at transport level (gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE / connect ECONNREFUSED to the ad ClusterIP, and 15s timeouts), which an application-level failure injection does not explain.

Likely causal chain (not a single-scope fact): ad's GetAds handler was starved by CPU-limit contention on the newly created ad container (usage pinned at the 50m limit, 96.9-99.2% CFS throttling from 13:17:13), which turned each of its ~12 per-request flag resolutions into 0.7-4.4s waits, making GetAds take 15-22s; frontend then exceeded the proxy's 15s route timeout (frontend-proxy ingress 504) or failed its ad RPC (500 -> proxy 500), producing the RequestErrorRate alert. The correlation is strong but the mechanism inside ad (why its CPU demand rose) is not directly observed.

Remaining candidate for the trigger of ad's CPU demand increase: a feature-flag driven CPU/GC stress in ad (flagd-config defines adHighCpu and adManualGc, both default 'off') or a new-pod startup behaviour after the 13:15:33Z rollout restart; this cannot be confirmed because the live flag state flagd served (the pod's config-rw volume) and any configuration change history are not readable in this Run.

Impact grouping as observed: affected are frontend-proxy (own ingress/egress ERROR spans with 504/503/500 and an error-rate burst) and frontend (own 500 ERROR spans on /api/data and gRPC AdService/GetAds, 3.75 error spans/s at 13:23:13) plus the ad workload itself (own GetAds span duration 20.77s, ad GetAds p95 6834ms, 99.2% CFS throttling); flagd was checked and appears healthy (0% throttling, 25-112us handler spans); load-generator spans only mirror the proxy/frontend failures as HTTP 500/504 callers (e.g. 'user_get_ads' GET 504 at 15.0s) and no fault was observed in it; no other service showed a positive ERROR span rate at 13:23:13.

gaps: The alert's own rule/expression could not be inspected: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data (evidence 7aeaf21d-5692-4de5-9596-bdfe7fe0a1c1-t0:765492f2-49c5-4c8b-bc03-70fa69a94972), so the annotation value 'current: 2.4555555555555553' and the alert start 13:14:13Z could not be reproduced from available series; the observed error burst begins ~13:17:13, so the difference between alert-start time and burst onset is unexplained.

Why the new ad container's CPU demand rose ~6-10x over the previous pod is unknown: the live flag values flagd served are held in the flagd pod's config-rw volume (not readable) and the change_history integration is not available, so flag toggles or other configuration changes around 13:15-13:17 cannot be verified.

Whether the ad pod was temporarily removed from Service ad's endpoints (which would explain the grpc-js 'connect ECONNREFUSED' to the ClusterIP) cannot be verified: stored events in otel-demo for the window contain no Unhealthy/probe-failure events for ad, and pod condition history is not available.

Node/CPU saturation at the hypervisor level is not measurable here: only container_cpu_* series exist (no node_cpu/node_load series were returned), so node-level CPU contention cannot be ruled out by metrics, only by the per-pod throttling comparison.

Trace, span-group and throttling readings come from sampled/aggregated views (Jaeger in-memory sample; traces_span_metrics_* count spans, not requests), so exact request-level error percentages for frontend-proxy are not established.

The adFailure flag defaultVariant 'on' in ConfigMap flagd-config could not be reconciled with the live behaviour; whether ad ever returned application-level failures during the window is unverified (ad spans carried no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series and only the newest 40 ad log lines were visible).
next_steps: Inspect Deployment ad (otel-demo) pod template CPU request/limit (10m/50m) against the ~0.05 core demand seen at 13:21-13:25 and decide whether to raise the limit or fix the workload behaviour that increased CPU demand.

Review why Deployment ad was rollout-restarted at 2026-11-16T13:15:33Z (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt) and who performed it, using the change-history/audit integration that is not available in this Run.
Read the flagd flag state and its change log (adHighCpu, adManualGc, adFailure) around 13:10-13:30 to test whether a flag toggle caused the ad CPU spike.
Correlate ad readiness-probe outcomes at 13:15-13:30 (kubelet probe logs / endpoint churn) to confirm whether ad left Service ad endpoints and caused the connect-refused failures.
Re-check frontend-proxy ingress error rate after 13:33Z to confirm the alert clears, and validate the RequestErrorRate rule expression/Alertmanager wiring against the actual series.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
